name: Ariel Kaye
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: Ariel's family once moved with their possessions spread across three neighbors' kitchens. Every inventory she makes now starts by asking what somebody needs on their first night and only then considers what it costs to replace. On Thursday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Ariel likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: The housing photographs kept cropping the tank out. I measured the bit of pavement the family suddenly occupied. I want that measurement in the appeal beside the flat's floor area.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Ariel has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Ariel starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Ariel has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To get the pavement inventory admitted to the tenant's appeal.
family: Desmond Calloway is Ariel’s half-sibling. Ariel chooses the familiar route. Desmond can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Desmond says, “I can drive but never had a chance to sit the test.”
connections: Harriet Sloan. The manager's abandonment inventory and the advocate's pavement measurements tell different stories about the same home.

reactions.situation: A reporter asks which neighbor held the aquarium key
reactions.response: Ariel asks whether the tenant wants the key holder named before saying anything to the reporter.
